summary.text: Opal is silica holding water in a non-crystalline structure, so it is classed as a mineraloid rather than a mineral.
Precious opal flashes shifting colours because tiny silica spheres stacked in a regular lattice diffract the light passing through it.
Opal too thin to stand alone is backed with dark material as a doublet, or also capped with clear quartz or plastic as a triplet.

items.prompt: Quartz and opal are both made of silica, but only quartz is called a mineral. What sets opal apart?

options.label: It is made by living things
Its atoms lack a crystal structure
It forms only on other planets
It contains no oxygen at all

items.explain: Opal is amorphous, not crystalline, so it is classed as a mineraloid while crystalline forms of silica are minerals.

items.prompt: You tilt a precious opal under a lamp and colours flash across it. What inside the stone makes this happen?

options.label: Specks of coloured metal scattered through it
Dyes absorbed from surrounding rock
Regularly packed silica spheres diffracting light
Air bubbles reflecting the lamp

items.explain: Ordered spheres of silica cause interference and diffraction of light, producing play-of-color.

items.prompt: Two precious opals differ only in how evenly their tiny silica spheres are sized and stacked. Which is likely the better gem?

options.label: The one with more uniform, regular spheres
The one with the most varied sphere sizes
Neither, because only colour matters
The one with the fewest spheres

items.explain: How regular the spheres' sizes and packing are is a prime factor in the quality of precious opal.

items.prompt: A jeweller backs a thin slice of precious opal with black ironstone. What does the dark layer do?

options.label: Hides cracks so the stone can be sold as natural
Makes the play of colour stand out more
Adds water to stop the opal drying out
Turns common opal into precious opal

items.explain: In a doublet, the darker backing emphasizes the play of color, giving a better display than a lighter backing.

items.prompt: Why should someone wearing a precious opal ring take care around heat?

options.label: Heat melts the silica spheres
Heat makes the opal turn black
Its water content makes it sensitive to heat
Heat releases toxic gases from it

items.explain: Opal's relatively high water content makes it sensitive to heat, which limits its jewellery uses.

items.prompt: A milky opal shows a hazy sheen but no flashes of colour. What kind of opal is it?

options.label: A triplet opal
A black opal
A precious opal
A common opal

items.explain: Common opal lacks play-of-color and often shows a hazy-milky sheen, which gemologists call opalescence.
